mekki-muskil:6-7.t: His saying, the Exalted: (بعاد إرم): (إرم) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of (عاد), or as a badal (substitute); the meaning of (إرم) is "the ancient". Whoever makes (إرم) a city assumes an omission in the speech, its implied form being "with the city of ʿĀd, Iram". It is also said that its implied form is "with ʿĀd, the owner of Iram"; on this view (إرم) is a definite feminine noun, which is why it is a diptote. (عاد) is fully declinable because it is masculine and light. It has been said that Iram is a great city existing at this time; it is also said that it is Alexandria, and also said that it is Damascus.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying (صفا صفا): a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying (وثمود الذين): [(ثمود)] is a diptote because it is the name of the tribe and is definite; its position is genitive by conjunction with (عاد). (الذين) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of (ثمود), or in the position of the accusative with "I mean" (أعني), or in the position of the nominative with an implied (هم).
His saying (ولا يحضون على طعام المسكين): the object of (يحضون) is omitted, its implied form being "and they do not urge people", or "themselves", or the like, "to feed the poor". Whoever reads it (تحاضون) does not assume the omission of an object; it is only "you urge one another among yourselves to good", and it is intransitive. [Translator's note: these comments concern verses 15–18 and 20 although the entry is keyed to verse 22; translated as written.]

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying (وجيء يومئذ بجهنم): (بجهنم) is in the position of the nominative as the object whose agent is not named [nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. It is also said that the maṣdar (verbal noun) is implied and is the object whose agent is not named. It may also be that the [deputy] object is (يومئذ).
His saying (يومئذ): a badal (substitute) from the first one. It is also said that its governor is (يتذكر).
His saying (وأنى له الذكرى): [(الذكرى)] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أنى) is the khabar (predicate).
